text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London finished at new nine-month highs after chasing a fresh New York rally. London's benchmark March breached the $1,800-mark to hit a session high of $,1820 per tonne, but then fell back to close at exactly $1,800 per tonne, up $95 from Tuesday. May added $82 to close at $1,780 per tonne.

In New York arabica futures continued to rise in another hectic session amid unchanged fundamentals. Present open interest is significantly higher than nearby availability of coffee and there is concern of a March squeeze ahead of expiry later this month as there is still very little certified coffee to meet delivery. Certified coffee stocks on March 4 were a mere 19,045 bags.

Traders said that prices will move higher until new supplies are drawn out or demand slows. However, before consumption slows there will probably be a period of increased demand due to hoarding and this too will need to be covered. Producers have little coffee left to offer for the remainder of the year and roasters need to buy not only to fill the pipeline but also to cover demand.

The latest ICO data show that producers have sold aggressively over the past few months, but that apparently failed to halt the upward trend. March added 8.10 cents/lb to close at 219.75 cents/lb, while May closed 5.40 cents/lb higher at 200.65 cents/lb.

ICO - Coffee exports by exporting members of the International Coffee Organization rose to 6.872 million 60-kg bags in January 1997 from 6.115 million bags the same month the previous year, the International Coffee Organization said. That brought total exports in October/January 1996/97 up to 26.217 million bags, up 11 per cent from the 23.644 million bags shipped the same period in 1995/96.

Brazil's market share in October/January 1996/97 rose dramatically to 27.46 per cent, up from 20.92 per cent in 1995/96. Colombia's market share rose to 15.78 per cent from 14.46 per cent in October/January 1995/96.

COSTA RICA - According to trade sources Costa Rica has sold the entire ACPC January/June 1997 export quota of 1.067 million 60-kg bags and exporters are now only negotiating positions for July and beyond. According to ICO figures the country exported 596,111 bags in October/January 1996/97, down from 734,649 bags the same period in 1995/96.

It was said the forward selling has resulted in Costa Rica exporting coffee at an average price well below the more than 200 cents/lb coffee is currently trading for at the New York coffee and sugar exchange. Cost Rica and El Salvador are hoping to see their export quotas for January/June rise as they take over portions of the quotas Honduras and Nicaragua and possibly Ecuador are unable to fill due to crop shortfalls, it was added.

POLAND - Poland imported 126,250 bags of coffee in September 1996, nearly 12 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.219 million bags, 8 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 6.5 per cent to 1.536 million bags.

Main suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Ivory Coast (153,800 vs 146,700 bags), India (138,900 vs 79,200 bags), Indonesia (263,600 vs 136,100 bags) and Vietnam (148,300 vs 211,900 bags).

The country exported 61,300 bags of coffee in January/September 1996, which compares to 34,400 bags the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 rose to 42,300 bags from 17,000 bags the previous year.

CANADA - Canada imported 241,329 bags of coffee in November 1996, below last year's figure of 272,600 bags. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 2.521 million bags, 9 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 11 per cent to 2.510 million bags.
Main suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Mexico (224,400 vs 119,000 bags), Brazil (269,200 vs 248,500 bags) and Colombia (434,100 vs 354,100 bags).

The country exported 317,600 bags of coffee in January/November 1996, 15 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped to 303,800 bags from 334,400 bags the previous year.
